name: Vue
purpose: keeps a page and the data behind it in step, so a change in one shows up in the other without being copied across by hand

name: React
purpose: builds a page out of small reusable pieces and redraws only the pieces whose data changed

name: jQuery
purpose: made reaching into a page short and made it work the same in every browser, at a time when it did not
note: Its own success retired it: what it added has since been built into the browsers themselves.

name: Angular
purpose: gives a large application its whole structure — routing, forms and data — rather than leaving it to be assembled

name: Bootstrap
purpose: supplies a set of ready-made appearances, so a page looks tidy and works on a phone without anybody designing it
note: The reason a great many sites of the 2010s look faintly alike.

name: Hibernate
purpose: moves objects in a program into the rows of a database and back, so nobody writes the SQL for it by hand

name: Spring
purpose: hands a program the parts it needs instead of letting it fetch them itself, which is what makes those parts exchangeable

name: Struts
purpose: separated a web application's pages from its logic, back when most of them had those mixed together
note: A great many Java web applications were built on it around 2005, and a fair number of them are still running.

name: Django
purpose: brings a database, an administration screen and the pages along with it, so a working site exists before anything is written

name: Laravel
purpose: gives PHP the structure it never had of its own, and is what most new PHP applications are built with
